as_told.title: Marconi's transatlantic signal bounced off the ionosphere

plain: Guglielmo Marconi's 1901 radio signal from Newfoundland to Cornwall crossed the Atlantic only because, without his knowing it, the waves bounced off the ionosphere, a charged layer high in the atmosphere, and came back down to the receiver. That is how a scientist named Filippo Biondi, who studies what lies beneath the pyramids, explains it on the show, drawing on James Clerk Maxwell's theory of electromagnetic waves. Michels later repeats Biondi's point in his own words, calling Marconi "ignorant in an adaptive way": too unaware of the problem to know it shouldn't work, so he tried it anyway and it did.
